tools.name: update_widget_code
tools.title: Write the code of an IDE widget placed on a layout
tools.description: Write the HTML, CSS and JavaScript of an IDE widget placed on a page or in a site container, in the current user's draft: a branded banner, a KPI tile, a custom form. Exactly one of page_ref and site_id names the layout; application_id is the id get_page_layout or get_site returned for the widget's window (the user's draft when they have one, the published layout otherwise); any other application, a section, a cell or a container is refused. Each of html, css and js replaces that part of the widget's code; a part omitted or null is kept; at least one is given; each is limited to the configured size (1 MB by default). Reserved to platform administrators, as the widget editor is, because the code runs in every visitor's browser; the user must also be able to edit the page or the site. The code is part of the draft: on the first write of a draft session the widget shared with the published layout is copied for the draft window, which then points at its own copy, and the published layout keeps rendering the previous code until publish_layout; discard_layout_draft starts again from the published layout; an unpublished copy is readable by the layout's editors only. The first draft of a page needs the right to edit the site's navigation, as opening the editor does. This write is one of the delivery's declared exceptions to all-or-nothing: the copy is created, then the window is pointed at it; when that second step fails the copy is deleted and the window keeps its previous code. Returns the window's application_id on the draft, the widget_id it now renders, the three parts of its code and draft_created; when draft_created is true, read the layout again for its ids.

page_ref.description: The page reference as get_page_layout and list_site_pages answer it (type::site::page), for a widget placed on a page; omit when site_id is given

site_id.description: The site id as list_sites and get_site answer it, for a widget placed in a site container; omit when page_ref is given

application_id.description: The application_id of the widget's window, as get_page_layout or get_site answered it

html.description: The widget's HTML, replacing the current one; omit to keep it

css.description: The widget's CSS, replacing the current one; omit to keep it

js.description: The widget's JavaScript, replacing the current one, run in every visitor's browser once published; omit to keep it

tools.name: get_site_static_resources
tools.title: Read the custom CSS and JavaScript of a site
tools.description: Read the custom CSS and JavaScript files of a site, the static resources Site Management lists for it: the styles and scripts added to every page of the site beyond what the theme and the styling tools cover. site_id is the id list_sites and get_site answer, of a portal site Site Management lists: a group site, a space's site or a space's public site is refused. Returns site_id and resources, each with its resource_id, its type (CSS or JS), its name, its content, its position (START_OF_HEAD, END_OF_HEAD, START_OF_BODY or END_OF_BODY, where it is added in the page; END_OF_BODY when none was chosen) and enabled (false: kept but not rendered). An empty resources list means the site has no custom CSS or JavaScript; it is not a refusal. Reserved to platform administrators, as in Site Management. Resources are attached to the site's name: the ones of the meta site (the platform's main site) are also rendered on the sites its navigation shows and on space sites. A refusal names the argument at fault and what to send instead: correct the call and try again.

site_id.description: The id of a portal site, as list_sites and get_site answer it

tools.name: set_site_static_resource
tools.title: Write a custom CSS or JavaScript file of a site
tools.description: Create a custom CSS or JavaScript file on a site, or update one: the static resources Site Management lists, added to every page of the site, for styles and scripts the theme and the styling tools do not cover. site_id names a portal site Site Management lists: a group site, a space's site or a space's public site is refused. Without resource_id a resource is created: type (CSS or JS), name and content are required, position defaults to END_OF_BODY and enabled to true. With resource_id, as get_site_static_resources answered it for this site, that resource is updated: each of name, content, position and enabled replaces the stored value, one omitted is kept, at least one is given, and type cannot change. content replaces the whole file, so read it first and send it back complete; it is limited to the configured size (1 MB by default). position is START_OF_HEAD, END_OF_HEAD, START_OF_BODY or END_OF_BODY. To stop rendering a resource without losing it, send enabled false; deleting one is done in Site Management. The change is not part of a draft: it is live on the site at once, for every visitor, and publish_layout and discard_layout_draft do not apply to it. Reserved to platform administrators, as in Site Management, because the code runs in every visitor's browser. Resources are attached to the site's name: the ones of the meta site (the platform's main site) are also rendered on the sites its navigation shows and on space sites. Returns the resource as saved: resource_id, type, name, content, position and enabled. A refusal names the argument at fault and what to send instead: correct the call and try again.

site_id.description: The id of a portal site, as list_sites and get_site answer it

resource_id.description: The resource_id get_site_static_resources answered for this site, to update that resource; omit to create one

type.description: CSS or JS; required to create a resource; on an update omit it, a resource's type cannot change

name.description: The resource's name as Site Management lists it, at most 255 characters; required to create a resource; omit to keep it on an update

content.description: The whole CSS or JavaScript of the resource, replacing the current one, live for every visitor at once; required to create a resource; omit to keep it on an update

position.description: Where the resource is added in the page: START_OF_HEAD, END_OF_HEAD, START_OF_BODY or END_OF_BODY; omit for END_OF_BODY on a creation and to keep it on an update

enabled.description: Whether the resource is rendered; omit for true on a creation and to keep it on an update
